requirement:
{impl}`requirements.configuration.feature_sections`
An item has recent coverage when it has a reference that covers it under
{cite}`requirements.references.rust_item_coverage`, or when its outline node, or
an outline node containing it, is named by file and selector in the inputs of
any version of an existing evidence record, citation review, or site review in
its coverage window. A file's coverage window MUST be its current contents on
disk, committed or not, together with its contents in each of the last N
commits in its Git history that changed it, read through a Git library rather
than by running `git`. A recorded hash MUST NOT matter here: an earlier version
names the node, whatever its code was then. N MUST be the workspace
`[coverage]` setting `reauthorings`, a positive integer, and 3 when it is not
set. When the history is unavailable, such as outside Git or in a shallow clone
missing those commits, the window MUST be the commits that are available, and
`habeas status --coverage` MUST say that coverage history is incomplete.
rationale:
The reviewed tests cover every obligation in `requirements.references.coverage.history`, and I found no gap. I read `src/coverage_history.rs#impl[RecentCoverage]/fn[add_history]` only to check how the window counts commits.

**Obligations and the tests that check them**
- **Which nodes count as covered (file and selector, any record kind, enclosing nodes).**
  - `tests/references.rs#fn[items_named_by_recent_evidence_have_recent_coverage_whatever_their_hash]` uses an ordinary record, a citation review that names an `impl` block containing a method, and a site review. It asserts that only the unread function warns.
  - The same test covers a stale recorded hash, which must not matter, and edits to read items.
  - `src/coverage_history.rs#mod[tests]/fn[coverage_follows_the_outline_parent_chain_not_selector_text]` checks the enclosing-node chain. It includes the root `""`, a different file, and a `/` inside brackets that must not count as a parent.
- **Window = current disk contents plus the last N commits that changed the file.**
  - `tests/coverage.rs#fn[coverage_lasts_for_three_reauthorings_of_the_record_that_read_an_item]` pins the default N of 3 at the boundary. After 2 re-authorings `parse` is still covered by the oldest version, and after the 3rd it warns. That excludes both N−1 and N+1 windows.
  - `tests/coverage.rs#fn[uncommitted_records_count_as_they_are_on_disk]` covers uncommitted contents. A re-authored record that drops `parse` leaves the committed version covering it, and a new on-disk record covers `render` before any commit.
  - `tests/coverage.rs#fn[deleting_the_only_record_that_read_an_item_warns_at_once]` covers a deleted record, which has no window.
  - `tests/coverage.rs#fn[a_merge_counts_only_when_it_differs_from_every_parent]` shows that a commit which does not change the file does not use up the window. With N=2, a merge that takes the side version unchanged still leaves the first version in the window.
- **N is the `[coverage]` `reauthorings` setting, positive, default 3.**
  - `tests/coverage.rs#fn[the_window_follows_the_workspace_setting]` sets N=1 and expects the older version to drop out. It also expects an error naming `coverage.reauthorings` for a value of 0.
  - `tests/coverage.rs#fn[an_invalid_coverage_table_is_a_validation_finding_but_authoring_proceeds]` checks 0, a string, and an unknown key.
- **History is read through a Git library, not by running `git`.**
  - `tests/coverage.rs#fn[coverage_history_uses_the_git_library_without_launching_git]` puts a stub `git` on `PATH` that fails and records any history command. `status --coverage` still gives correct warnings and the stub is never invoked.
  - `tests/coverage.rs#fn[validation_does_not_read_git_history]` is also relevant.
- **Unavailable history uses the available commits, and `status --coverage` says history is incomplete.**
  - Shallow clones: `tests/coverage.rs#fn[a_shallow_clone_uses_the_history_it_has_and_says_so]`, `tests/coverage.rs#fn[status_shows_coverage_warnings_and_says_when_history_is_incomplete]`, and `tests/coverage.rs#fn[incomplete_history_is_noted_even_with_nothing_to_warn_about]`. The last one covers incomplete history with no warnings.
  - Shallow clones that hold every window, a linked worktree of a shallow clone, and an uncommitted record on a full shallow history: `tests/coverage.rs#fn[a_shallow_clone_holding_every_window_is_complete]`, `tests/coverage.rs#fn[a_linked_worktree_of_a_shallow_clone_knows_where_history_ends]`, and `tests/coverage.rs#fn[an_uncommitted_record_does_not_make_a_full_shallow_history_incomplete]`.
  - Other unavailable-history cases: `tests/coverage.rs#fn[outside_git_only_the_files_on_disk_count_and_history_is_incomplete]` (outside Git), `tests/coverage.rs#fn[an_unreadable_historical_version_makes_history_incomplete]` (missing blob), and `tests/coverage.rs#fn[an_unlistable_evidence_directory_makes_history_incomplete]` (unlistable evidence directory).
  - The `incomplete` flag and the status text are both asserted.
- **Examples** `coverage.reauthored`, `coverage.deleted_requirement`, `coverage.uncommitted`, and `coverage.shallow_clone` are each exercised by the tests above. Those tests carry the matching `{test}` references.

The remaining marked tests are `src/commands.rs#mod[tests]/fn[coverage_warning_inventory_matches_full_inspection_with_invalid_evidence]` and `tests/authoring_batch.rs#fn[dumb_terminal_keeps_plain_batch_diagnostics]`. They check that the warning inventory is consistent and that the batch output gives only the count, so they supplement the rest.

I found no unmarked relevant tests, no missing assertions, and no acknowledged gaps to evaluate.

text: :::{req} coverage.history
{impl}`requirements.configuration.feature_sections`
An item has recent coverage when it has a reference that covers it under
{cite}`requirements.references.rust_item_coverage`, or when its outline node, or
an outline node containing it, is named by file and selector in the inputs of
any version of an existing evidence record, citation review, or site review in
its coverage window. A file's coverage window MUST be its current contents on
disk, committed or not, together with its contents in each of the last N
commits in its Git history that changed it, read through a Git library rather
than by running `git`. A recorded hash MUST NOT matter here: an earlier version
names the node, whatever its code was then. N MUST be the workspace
`[coverage]` setting `reauthorings`, a positive integer, and 3 when it is not
set. When the history is unavailable, such as outside Git or in a shallow clone
missing those commits, the window MUST be the commits that are available, and
`habeas status --coverage` MUST say that coverage history is incomplete.
:::{req} rust_item_coverage

During repository validation, Habeas MUST parse every first-party Rust source file: every `.rs` file among the sources reference discovery considers under {cite}`requirements.references.discovery`, except those under the project-root `vendor` directory. Each explicitly declared function or method, including trait methods and test helpers, and each struct, enum, and union is an item that can be covered. An item is covered when it has a valid `{impl}`, `{cite}`, or `{test}` reference to a defined requirement or named example, or a valid citation of the built-in `habeas:util` under {cite}`requirements.references.util`, in a Rust comment attached to it or within its body; or when its outline node, or an outline node containing it, is recorded with its current hash as an outline input of an evidence record, a citation review, or a site review. Outline inputs recorded from selected search snippets under {cite}`requirements.authoring.finish_search.inputs` MUST count alongside mandatory inputs and additional reads. Comments belong to items under {cite}`requirements.references.outline_comments`; a comment before a field, variant, or attribute inside an item belongs to that item. A named example MUST reference a requirement under {cite}`requirements.examples.definition`. A reference in a string literal, on an enclosing module or impl block, or only in an evidence input MUST NOT count for the items it encloses. Habeas MUST report a Rust parse failure instead of silently skipping the file. Only {cite}`requirements.references.coverage.tests` and {cite}`requirements.references.coverage.examples` make an uncovered item a validation error; other items without recent coverage are warned about under {cite}`requirements.references.coverage.report`.
:::{example} coverage.reauthored
Function `parse` has no reference, and the evidence of `requirements.cli.check`
read it. The requirement is re-authored and committed twice, and neither new
record reads `parse`. With the default window of 3, the record's third most
recent version still names `parse`, so `habeas status --coverage` does not warn.
After a third such commit, no version in the window names it, and
`habeas status --coverage` warns about `parse`.
{test}`requirements.references.coverage.history`
{test}`requirements.references.coverage.report`
:::{example} coverage.deleted_requirement
Function `render` is read only by the evidence of `requirements.cli.render`.
The requirement and its evidence file are deleted.
Deleted files have no coverage window, so `habeas status --coverage` warns about
`render` at once, before any further commit.
{test}`requirements.references.coverage.history`
:::{example} coverage.uncommitted
The evidence of `requirements.cli.check` read `parse`. The requirement is
re-authored but not yet committed, and the new record does not read `parse`.
The committed versions in the window still name it, so
`habeas status --coverage` does not warn. If the new record had read `parse`,
its contents on disk would cover it even before the commit.
{test}`requirements.references.coverage.history`
:::{example} coverage.shallow_clone
In a shallow clone with no history beyond the last commit, each window holds
only the files' contents on disk and in that commit. `habeas status --coverage`
says that coverage history is incomplete and warns about items those contents
do not cover. {test}`requirements.references.coverage.history`
